From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Spanish football manager (born 1970)
For other people named Luis Enrique, see [Luis Enrique (disambiguation)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique_\(disambiguation\) "Luis Enrique \(disambiguation\)").
In this [Spanish name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_name "Spanish name"), the first or paternal [surname](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surname "Surname") is _[Martínez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mart%C3%ADnez_\(surname\) "Martínez \(surname\)")_ and the second or maternal family name is _[García](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garc%C3%ADa_\(surname\) "García \(surname\)")_.

**Luis Enrique Martínez García** (Spanish pronunciation: [[lwis enˈrike maɾˈtineθ ɡaɾˈθia]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Spanish "Help:IPA/Spanish")[football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") [manager](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manager_\(association_football\) "Manager \(association football\)") and former player who is the head coach of [Ligue 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ligue_1 "Ligue 1") club [Paris Saint-Germain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Saint-Germain_FC "Paris Saint-Germain FC").
A versatile player with good technique, he was capable of playing in several positions but was usually deployed as a [midfielder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midfielder "Midfielder") or [forward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_\(association_football\) "Forward \(association football\)"), and was also noted for his temperament and stamina. Starting in 1988 and ending in 2004, he began his career at [Sporting de Gijón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sporting_de_Gij%C3%B3n "Sporting de Gijón") and later represented both [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF") and [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona") with both individual and team success, taking part in 558 official games and scoring 144 goals. He appeared with the [Spain national team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain_men's_national_football_team "Spain men's national football team") in three [World Cups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup "FIFA World Cup") and [Euro 1996](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_1996 "UEFA Euro 1996").
Luis Enrique started working as a manager in 2008 with [Barcelona B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona_Atl%C3%A8tic "FC Barcelona Atlètic"), before moving to [Roma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Roma "AS Roma") three years later. In the [2013–14 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_La_Liga "2013–14 La Liga"), he managed [Celta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RC_Celta_de_Vigo "RC Celta de Vigo"), before returning to Barcelona and winning the [treble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treble_\(association_football\) "Treble \(association football\)") in his [first year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_La_Liga "2014–15 La Liga") and the [double](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_\(association_football\) "Double \(association football\)") in [the second](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_La_Liga "2015–16 La Liga"). In 2018, he was appointed Spain head coach for the first time before resigning for family reasons in 2019, but reassumed the position the same year and subsequently led the team to the semi-finals of [Euro 2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2020 "UEFA Euro 2020") and to second place in the [2020–21 Nations League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020%E2%80%9321_UEFA_Nations_League "2020–21 UEFA Nations League"), resigning at the end of the [2022 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup "2022 FIFA World Cup"). In July 2023, he joined French club Paris Saint-Germain, claiming three trophies in his first season and four in his second, including the [first UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2025 UEFA Champions League final") in their history, a title he retained the [following campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2026 UEFA Champions League final").
## Club career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luis_Enrique&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Club career")]
Luis Enrique was born in [Gijón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gij%C3%B3n "Gijón"), [Asturias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asturias "Asturias"), and began his career with local [Sporting de Gijón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sporting_de_Gij%C3%B3n "Sporting de Gijón"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-2) where he gained the nickname _Lucho_ after [Luis Flores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Flores_\(Mexican_footballer\) "Luis Flores \(Mexican footballer\)"), a Mexican forward in the team.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-Normal-3) He then spent most of his playing days with the two biggest Spanish clubs: first [Real Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Madrid_CF "Real Madrid CF") for five seasons and,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-4) in 1996, after seeing out his contract and notably scoring in a 5–0 home win against [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona") in January 1995, stating later he "rarely felt appreciated by the Real Madrid supporters and didn't have good memories there",[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-Memories-5) he moved to their fierce rivals at the [Camp Nou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Nou "Camp Nou") on a [free transfer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_transfer_\(association_football\) "Free transfer \(association football\)").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-6) The Catalans' supporters were at first hesitant about their new acquisition, but he soon won the hearts of the _[culers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supporters_of_FC_Barcelona "Supporters of FC Barcelona")_ , staying eight years, eventually becoming [team captain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_\(association_football\) "Captain \(association football\)") and scoring several times in _[El Clásico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Cl%C3%A1sico "El Clásico")_ against his former employers;[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-7) he passionately [celebrated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goal_celebration "Goal celebration") at the [Santiago Bernabéu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santiago_Bernab%C3%A9u_Stadium "Santiago Bernabéu Stadium"), where he grabbed his jersey after a 25-yard strike that beat the opposing goalkeeper.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-8)
Luis Enrique scored 46 [La Liga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Liga "La Liga") goals in his first three seasons with Barcelona,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-10) with the side finishing runner-up in [1996–97](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996%E2%80%9397_La_Liga "1996–97 La Liga") and subsequently winning back-to-back domestic championship accolades. Furthermore, he was named Spanish [Player of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Player_of_the_year_award "Player of the year award") by _[El País](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Pa%C3%ADs "El País")_ in [the following campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997%E2%80%9398_La_Liga "1997–98 La Liga").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-Memories-5)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-RSSSF-11) He also scored the opening goal in the [1997 UEFA Super Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1997_UEFA_Super_Cup "1997 UEFA Super Cup"), a 3–1 aggregate triumph against [Borussia Dortmund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Borussia_Dortmund "Borussia Dortmund").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-USC-12)
During his final years in Barcelona, Luis Enrique was often injured, and did not want to renew his contract. He had been offered a deal by his first club Sporting, which he, however, declined, stating that "he wouldn't be able to reach the level he demanded of himself" and that "he wouldn't be doing Sporting much of a favour by going there."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-Bows-13) His concerns about his level and fitness made him retire on 10 August 2004 at the age of 34,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-Bows-13) and he finished his professional career with league totals of 400 games and 102 goals, being named by [Pelé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pel%C3%A9 "Pelé") as one of the [top 125 greatest living footballers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_100 "FIFA 100") in March.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-BBC-14)
## International career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luis_Enrique&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: International career")]
Luis Enrique played for [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain_men's_national_football_team "Spain men's national football team") in three [FIFA World Cups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup "FIFA World Cup"): [1994](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_FIFA_World_Cup "1994 FIFA World Cup"), [1998](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1998_FIFA_World_Cup "1998 FIFA World Cup") and [2002](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_FIFA_World_Cup "2002 FIFA World Cup") (as well as [UEFA Euro 1996](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_1996 "UEFA Euro 1996")), and scored 12 goals while earning 62 [caps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cap_\(sport\) "Cap \(sport\)"). He was also a member of the [gold-winning squad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_at_the_1992_Summer_Olympics "Football at the 1992 Summer Olympics") at the [1992 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics "1992 Summer Olympics") in [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barcelona "Barcelona"),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-15) and made his debut for the main side on 17 April 1991, featuring for 22 minutes in a 0–2 [friendly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exhibition_game "Exhibition game") loss to [Romania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romania_national_football_team "Romania national football team") in [Cáceres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A1ceres,_Spain "Cáceres, Spain").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-16)
In the 1994 World Cup, held in the United States, Luis Enrique scored his first international goal, in the [round-of-16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-elimination_tournament "Single-elimination tournament") 3–0 win over [Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland_national_football_team "Switzerland national football team") in [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.")[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-17) In the 2–1 [quarter-final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1994_FIFA_World_Cup#Quarter-finals "1994 FIFA World Cup") defeat against [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy_national_football_team "Italy national football team") at the [Foxboro Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foxboro_Stadium "Foxboro Stadium"), [Mauro Tassotti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mauro_Tassotti "Mauro Tassotti")'s elbow made contact with Luis Enrique's face to bloody effect but the incident went unpunished during the match – Tassotti was banned for eight games afterwards;[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-19) Tassotti later stated he had instantly and deeply regretted his actions, describing them as "stupid" but not premeditated and purely instinctive since his shirt had been pulled by Luis Enrique, and the former personally apologised to the latter.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-20) Nonetheless, when Spain met Italy at [Euro 2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2008 "UEFA Euro 2008") on 22 June, to battle for a place in the semi-finals, Luis Enrique reportedly called for the team to "take revenge" for the 1994 World Cup incident by beating Italy.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-21) Tassotti, an assistant coach with [AC Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AC_Milan "AC Milan") at the time, told the newspaper _[Marca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marca_\(newspaper\) "Marca \(newspaper\)")_ that he was tired of always being reminded of this incident, and that he had never intended to hurt the Spaniard.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-22)
At the 1998 World Cup, Luis Enrique played a major role in a 6–1 rout of [Bulgaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulgaria_national_football_team "Bulgaria national football team") in the last game of the group, scoring and [assisting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assist_\(association_football\) "Assist \(association football\)") once and also winning a [penalty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_kick_\(association_football\) "Penalty kick \(association football\)"), but the Spaniards were eliminated nonetheless.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-23) On 5 June of the following year, he scored a [hat-trick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hat-trick_\(association_football\) "Hat-trick \(association football\)") in a 9–0 win in [Villarreal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villarreal "Villarreal") over [San Marino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Marino_national_football_team "San Marino national football team") in the [Euro 2000 qualifiers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2000_qualifying "UEFA Euro 2000 qualifying").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-24)
On 23 June 2002, Luis Enrique retired from international football, in order to give the younger players more playing time and focus only on his club.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-25)
## Style of play
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luis_Enrique&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Style of play")]
Having occupied several positions, Luis Enrique was most noted for his exceptional versatility and consistency. He was capable of playing anywhere in [midfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midfielder "Midfielder") or along the [front line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_\(association_football\) "Forward \(association football\)"), and was fielded in all positions on the pitch throughout his career, except those of [central defender](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_defender "Central defender") and [goalkeeper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goalkeeper_\(association_football\) "Goalkeeper \(association football\)"). His usual position was as an [attacking midfielder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attacking_midfielder "Attacking midfielder") in the centre of the pitch, due to his ability to link-up the forwards and the midfield, or as a [right winger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_winger "Right winger"), but he was capable of playing anywhere along the right flank, and was often deployed as an attacking [full-back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Full_back_\(association_football\) "Full back \(association football\)") or [wing-back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wing-back_\(association_football\) "Wing-back \(association football\)"), or even as a left winger on occasion.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-26)
Due to his keen eye for goal and ability to make attacking runs into the box, Luis Enrique frequently played as a forward, either in a withdrawn role as a [second striker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_\(association_football\)#Second_striker "Forward \(association football\)") behind the team's main goalscorer, or even as an out-and-out [striker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_\(association_football\)#Striker "Forward \(association football\)") or [centre-forward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forward_\(association_football\)#Centre-forward "Forward \(association football\)") – he was also used in deeper midfield roles. In addition to his playing abilities, he also stood out for his commitment, temperament, determination and leadership.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-Normal-3)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-36)
## Managerial career
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luis_Enrique&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Managerial career")]
### Barcelona B
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luis_Enrique&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Barcelona B")]
On 26 May 2008, Luis Enrique returned to Barcelona, taking over the reins of the [B team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona_Atl%C3%A8tic "FC Barcelona Atlètic"), renamed Barcelona Atlètic for [that season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_Segunda_Divisi%C3%B3n_B "2008–09 Segunda División B");[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-Reserves-37) as he succeeded long-time Barcelona teammate [Pep Guardiola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pep_Guardiola "Pep Guardiola"), he stated: "I have come home" and "I finished playing here and now I will start coaching here". He found success in his [second year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Segunda_Divisi%C3%B3n_B "2009–10 Segunda División B"), helping the club return to [Segunda División](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Segunda_Divisi%C3%B3n "Segunda División") after an absence of eleven years.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-38)
In mid-March 2011, Luis Enrique announced he would leave at the end of [the campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Segunda_Divisi%C3%B3n "2010–11 Segunda División"), despite still having two years left on his contract.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-39) He led the side to the playoffs, but they were ineligible for promotion.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-40)
### Roma
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luis_Enrique&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Roma")]
On 8 June 2011, Luis Enrique reached an agreement with Italian [Serie A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serie_A "Serie A") club [Roma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AS_Roma "AS Roma") to become the _Giallorossi_ 's new head coach. He signed a two-year contract and was joined by a staff of four members including [Iván de la Peña](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iv%C3%A1n_de_la_Pe%C3%B1a "Iván de la Peña"), who played two years for crosstown rivals [Lazio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SS_Lazio "SS Lazio"), as a technical collaborator.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-Roma1-41)
Roma were [eliminated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_UEFA_Europa_League "2011–12 UEFA Europa League") from the [UEFA Europa League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Europa_League "UEFA Europa League") by [Slovan Bratislava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C5%A0K_Slovan_Bratislava "ŠK Slovan Bratislava"), amid great discussion of the [substitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substitute_\(association_football\) "Substitute \(association football\)") of [Francesco Totti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francesco_Totti "Francesco Totti") for [Stefano Okaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stefano_Okaka "Stefano Okaka"). The [capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome "Rome")-based side also lost their first game in the [domestic league](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Serie_A "2011–12 Serie A") against [Cagliari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cagliari_Calcio "Cagliari Calcio"), making it just the third time that they lost the opener in 18 years.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-42)
Even though he still had two years remaining on his contract, Luis Enrique decided to leave Roma at the end of the season after failure to qualify for any [European competition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-Roma2-44)
### Celta
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luis_Enrique&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Celta")]
On 8 June 2013, Luis Enrique became [Celta de Vigo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RC_Celta_de_Vigo "RC Celta de Vigo")'s new manager, replacing former national teammate [Abel Resino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abel_Resino "Abel Resino").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-Celta1-45) He led the [Galicians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Galicia_\(Spain\) "Galicia \(Spain\)") to the ninth position in his [only season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_La_Liga "2013–14 La Liga"), highlights including a 2–0 home win against Real Madrid that ended the opposition's possibilities of winning the league title.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-46)
On 16 May 2014, Luis Enrique announced that he would be leaving Celta.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-Celta2-47)
### Barcelona
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luis_Enrique&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Barcelona")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b6/2015_UEFA_Super_Cup_66.jpg/250px-2015_UEFA_Super_Cup_66.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:2015_UEFA_Super_Cup_66.jpg)Luis Enrique with [Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Barcelona "FC Barcelona") at the [2015 UEFA Super Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Super_Cup "2015 UEFA Super Cup")
On 19 May 2014, Luis Enrique returned to Barcelona as a manager on a two-year deal. He was recommended by sporting director [Andoni Zubizarreta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andoni_Zubizarreta "Andoni Zubizarreta"), his former national teammate.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-Appoint-48) His first competitive match was a 3–0 home league win over [Elche](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elche_CF "Elche CF"), where he handed debuts to new signings [Claudio Bravo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claudio_Bravo "Claudio Bravo"), [Jérémy Mathieu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%A9r%C3%A9my_Mathieu "Jérémy Mathieu") and [Ivan Rakitić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Rakiti%C4%87 "Ivan Rakitić"), and gave youth products [Munir El Haddadi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munir_El_Haddadi "Munir El Haddadi"), [Rafinha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafinha_\(footballer,_born_February_1993\) "Rafinha \(footballer, born February 1993\)") and [Sandro Ramírez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandro_Ram%C3%ADrez "Sandro Ramírez") their maiden league appearances for the club, while summer signing [Luis Suárez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Su%C3%A1rez_\(Uruguayan_footballer\) "Luis Suárez \(Uruguayan footballer\)") was unavailable for selection due to suspension.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-49)
Luis Enrique suffered his first defeat in the competition on 25 October 2014, away against Real Madrid, and although Barcelona had a successful run in the year, his management came under scrutiny because of his tactics involving several lineup changes in consecutive games. Moreover, a quarrel with [Lionel Messi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi") and other players further accentuated the team's poor form.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-50)
Amid reports of dressing room unrest and after a defeat to [Real Sociedad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real_Sociedad "Real Sociedad"), Zubizarreta was dismissed in early January, weakening Luis Enrique's standing at the club. A significant upturn in form followed, as a result of the coach deciding on a settled lineup with a tweak in the formation: Messi and [Neymar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neymar "Neymar") now played as inverted wingers, while Suárez was the lone striker.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-Lowe-51)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-Pettigrove-52) He soon equaled Guardiola's record of eleven consecutive victories,[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-Pettigrove-52) while the side went on to beat [Atlético Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Madrid "Atlético Madrid") and [Villarreal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villarreal_CF "Villarreal CF") convincingly in the [Copa del Rey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_del_Rey "Copa del Rey") to [advance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Copa_del_Rey "2014–15 Copa del Rey") to [the final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Copa_del_Rey_final "2015 Copa del Rey final"). In the domestic league, after eight wins in nine matches, they returned to the top of the table after 15 weeks.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-53)
On 21 April 2015, Luis Enrique recorded his 42nd win after 50 games in charge of Barcelona with a 2–0 victory over [Paris Saint-Germain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Saint-Germain_FC "Paris Saint-Germain FC"), the best record of any manager.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-54) He went on to lead the club to [the final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_UEFA_Champions_League "2014–15 UEFA Champions League") of the [UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League") and, on 17 May, led it to its 23rd national championship with one match to spare following a 1–0 win at the [Vicente Calderón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vicente_Calder%C3%B3n_Stadium "Vicente Calderón Stadium") against Atlético Madrid.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-56) On 6 June, having earlier won the domestic cup against [Athletic Bilbao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Athletic_Bilbao "Athletic Bilbao") by the same score, the team sealed a [treble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treble_\(association_football\) "Treble \(association football\)") with a 3–1 defeat of [Juventus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juventus_FC "Juventus FC") in the [Champions League final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2015 UEFA Champions League final") in Berlin,[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-57) and three days later he signed a new contract until 2017.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-58)
On 11 August 2015, Barcelona won the [2015 UEFA Super Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_UEFA_Super_Cup "2015 UEFA Super Cup") 5–4 against [Sevilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-59) On 2 December, against [Villanovense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CF_Villanovense "CF Villanovense") in the [Copa del Rey round of 32](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015%E2%80%9316_Copa_del_Rey#Round_of_32 "2015–16 Copa del Rey"), Luis Enrique decided against bringing on a new player following Mathieu's injury with 12 minutes to go even though two replacements could still be made, as the score was 6–1 at that time and the manager said he did not want to risk introducing players to the game without adequate warm-up.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-60)
In his first two seasons, Luis Enrique rotated his goalkeepers, with Bravo playing league games and [Marc-André ter Stegen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc-Andr%C3%A9_ter_Stegen "Marc-André ter Stegen") playing cup and European matches. Both players, however, expressed opposition to this policy.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-62) A second [double](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double_\(association_football\) "Double \(association football\)") was achieved on 22 May 2016, following a [2–0 Copa del Rey victory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Copa_del_Rey_final "2016 Copa del Rey final") over [Sevilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sevilla_FC "Sevilla FC") after [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_\(sports\) "Overtime \(sports\)") in which the team played more than 50 minutes with one player less, following the [dismissal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ejection_\(sports\) "Ejection \(sports\)") of [Javier Mascherano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Javier_Mascherano "Javier Mascherano").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-63)
On 1 March 2017, Luis Enrique announced that he would not continue as team manager after 30 June on expiration of his contract.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-64)
### Spain
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luis_Enrique&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Spain")]
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a1/%D0%9E%D1%82%D0%BA%D1%80%D1%8B%D1%82%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D1%82%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%BD%D0%B8%D1%80%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%BA%D0%B0_%D1%81%D0%B1%D0%BE%D1%80%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%B9_%D0%98%D1%81%D0%BF%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%B8%D0%B8_%D0%BF%D0%B5%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%B4_%D0%BC%D0%B0%D1%82%D1%87%D0%B5%D0%BC_%D1%81%D0%BE_%D1%81%D0%B1%D0%BE%D1%80%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%B9_%D0%A3%D0%BA%D1%80%D0%B0%D0%B8%D0%BD%D1%8B._12_%D0%BE%D0%BA%D1%82%D1%8F%D0%B1%D1%80%D1%8F_2020_%D0%B3%D0%BE%D0%B4%D0%B0_%E2%80%94_1150788.jpg/250px-thumbnail.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:%D0%9E%D1%82%D0%BA%D1%80%D1%8B%D1%82%D0%B0%D1%8F_%D1%82%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%BD%D0%B8%D1%80%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%BA%D0%B0_%D1%81%D0%B1%D0%BE%D1%80%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%B9_%D0%98%D1%81%D0%BF%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%B8%D0%B8_%D0%BF%D0%B5%D1%80%D0%B5%D0%B4_%D0%BC%D0%B0%D1%82%D1%87%D0%B5%D0%BC_%D1%81%D0%BE_%D1%81%D0%B1%D0%BE%D1%80%D0%BD%D0%BE%D0%B9_%D0%A3%D0%BA%D1%80%D0%B0%D0%B8%D0%BD%D1%8B._12_%D0%BE%D0%BA%D1%82%D1%8F%D0%B1%D1%80%D1%8F_2020_%D0%B3%D0%BE%D0%B4%D0%B0_%E2%80%94_1150788.jpg)Luis Enrique managing [Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spain_national_football_team "Spain national football team") in 2020
Luis Enrique was named coach of the Spain national team on 9 July 2018, replacing former club and country teammate [Fernando Hierro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Hierro "Fernando Hierro").[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-65) His first match in charge occurred on 8 September, and he led the side to a 2–1 win against [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England_national_football_team "England national football team") in the [UEFA Nations League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_UEFA_Nations_League "2018–19 UEFA Nations League") at [Wembley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wembley_Stadium "Wembley Stadium").[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-66)
In November 2019, Luis Enrique rejoined the national team[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-67) after having quit his post for personal reasons four months prior.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-68)[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-69)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-70) Speaking to the press after his return, a visibly angry Luis Enrique alleged that his friend and colleague of six years [Robert Moreno](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Moreno "Robert Moreno") — who managed the national team after his resignation — was "disloyal" and wanted to hold on to his interim position.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-School-71)
When Luis Enrique selected a 24-man [Euro 2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2020 "UEFA Euro 2020") [squad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA_Euro_2020_squads "UEFA Euro 2020 squads") (despite being allowed 26) that contained no Real Madrid players, he was accused of having an anti-Madrid bias. Several high-profile omissions from his squad were seen as a way for him to assert control over the dressing room and the team.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-School-71) However, he led Spain to the tournament's semi-finals, in which they lost against Italy on [penalties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_\(association_football\) "Penalty shoot-out \(association football\)"), after a 1–1 draw.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-72)
At the [2022 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_FIFA_World_Cup "2022 FIFA World Cup"), Luis Enrique's team were defeated in the round of 16 following another shootout, 3–0 against [Morocco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morocco_national_football_team "Morocco national football team").[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-73) In the wake of this performance, he stepped down from his position.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-74)
### Paris Saint-Germain
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luis_Enrique&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Paris Saint-Germain")]
On 5 July 2023, Luis Enrique officially became the manager of [Ligue 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ligue_1 "Ligue 1") club Paris Saint-Germain, succeeding [Christophe Galtier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christophe_Galtier "Christophe Galtier");[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-75) he signed a two-year contract.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-76) He won a domestic treble in his [first season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_Paris_Saint-Germain_FC_season "2023–24 Paris Saint-Germain FC season"),[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-77) also reaching the [Champions League semi-finals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_UEFA_Champions_League "2023–24 UEFA Champions League").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-78)
PSG renewed their domestic supremacy in [2024–25](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_Ligue_1 "2024–25 Ligue 1"), losing no matches in the first 28 and winning the league with six to spare.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-PSGAngers-79) Luis Enrique also led them to [retain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024%E2%80%9325_Coupe_de_France "2024–25 Coupe de France") the [Coupe de France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coupe_de_France "Coupe de France")[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-CDF-80) and to the [final of the Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2025 UEFA Champions League final"),[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-81) where they beat [Inter Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter_Milan "Inter Milan") 5–0 to complete a [continental treble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treble_\(association_football\)#Continental_trebles "Treble \(association football\)"), the first by a French club, while he became the second manager to achieve this twice.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-UCL-82)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-83) He also guided the side to [the final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_FIFA_Club_World_Cup_final "2025 FIFA Club World Cup final") of the [2025 FIFA Club World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_FIFA_Club_World_Cup "2025 FIFA Club World Cup"), the first edition of the expanded competition, but lost 3–0 to [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C."), ending hopes of [claiming seven trophies in a calendar year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sextuple_\(association_football\)#Seventh_and_Eighth_Title "Sextuple \(association football\)") for the first time in history.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-84)
On 28 April 2026, Luis Enrique secured his 50th Champions League victory in just 77 matches, surpassing the previous record set by Guardiola who reached the milestone in 80.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-85) A month later, his side [claimed the French title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025%E2%80%9326_Ligue_1 "2025–26 Ligue 1") with a 2–0 win against [Lens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RC_Lens "RC Lens"), marking his third in the competition.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-86) He then guided Paris Saint-Germain to a 4–3 shootout victory over [Arsenal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arsenal_F.C. "Arsenal F.C.") in the [Champions League final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2026_UEFA_Champions_League_final "2026 UEFA Champions League final") following a 1–1 draw after extra time.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-87)
## Manager profile
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luis_Enrique&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Manager profile")]
### Tactics
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luis_Enrique&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Tactics")]
One of the most successful managers of his generation,[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-88)[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-89)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-90)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-91)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-92)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-93)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-94) Luis Enrique's incisive and direct football featuring quick transitions from defense to attack, though reliant on the front three of Messi, Suárez and [Neymar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neymar "Neymar"), was in sharp contrast to the possession-heavy approach of Barcelona managers immediately prior to him.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-95)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-96) Statistically, Luis Enrique's Barcelona, in his first two years at the club, were better than Guardiola's: Comparatively his team had scored more goals and conceded fewer, had a higher win percentage and won competitions at a similar rate.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-97) Guardiola hailed them as the best counter-attacking team in the world.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-Lowe-51)
In his first two seasons at the Camp Nou, Luis Enrique fielded a [4–3–3 formation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formation_\(association_football\) "Formation \(association football\)"). Results improved after he stopped changing his starting eleven. The team's creative outlet was the wings with Neymar and Messi as inside forwards flanking Suárez, a departure from their usual playing style. [Ivan Rakitić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Rakiti%C4%87 "Ivan Rakitić") played a pivotal role in transitioning defense to attack, and [Andrés Iniesta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9s_Iniesta "Andrés Iniesta")'s influence withered, while [Xavi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xavi_\(footballer,_born_1980\) "Xavi \(footballer, born 1980\)"), the club's captain, reduced to a part-time, [substitute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Substitute_\(association_football\) "Substitute \(association football\)") role. With overlapping full-backs offering width, Neymar and Messi often drifted in-field, encouraging midfielders, Rakitic and Iniesta, to move into channels and attack in and around the box. In his third and final year, struggling for form and results, the manager switched to a 3–4–3 offense morphing into a 4–4–2 defensive shape, reminiscent of [Antonio Conte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antonio_Conte "Antonio Conte")'s [Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premier_League "Premier League") winners [Chelsea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_F.C. "Chelsea F.C.") more than [Johan Cruyff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johan_Cruyff "Johan Cruyff")'s [Dream Team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barcelona_\(Dream_Team\) "Barcelona \(Dream Team\)"), with Messi at the top of a midfield diamond, acting as chief play-maker, and [Sergio Busquets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sergio_Busquets "Sergio Busquets"), the sole holding defensive midfielder, responsible for breaking the first-line of opposition press. The system favoured Neymar in particular, who played as a left forward, often cutting inside to link with lone striker Suárez, or to create an overload in the final-third sharing creative responsibilities with Messi. This change in formation was instrumental as they overcame 4–0, the biggest first-leg deficit in Champions League history, by [defeating PSG 6–1 in the second-leg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Remontada "La Remontada"); however, the physical and tactical discipline required to sustain a 3–4–3 proved controversial.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-School-71)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-CW-98)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-wingplay-99)[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-FW-100)[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-101)[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-102)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-103)
Luis Enrique continued to favour 4–3–3 for Spain, and at times the riskier 3–4–3 when the situation demanded, with the sole defensive midfielder in the pivot being the only commonality. Lacking the front three he had at Barcelona, his football retained positional and vertical aspects, though with box-to-box central midfielders, like [Koke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koke_\(footballer,_born_1992\) "Koke \(footballer, born 1992\)") or [Pedri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedri "Pedri"), offering attacking thrust while the center forward dropped deep to bring wide forwards into play, accompanied by overlapping full-backs who offer width. Whilst pressing oppositions high-up, the center forward, usually [Álvaro Morata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%81lvaro_Morata "Álvaro Morata"), screened the opposition defensive midfielder as wide forwards engaged opposition center backs. Spain's defensive midfielder, often Busquets, tracked the run of opposition attackers when they dropped deep, sometimes pressing higher than the team's other central midfielders. In possession, Spain usually started playing out from the back, to draw the opposition in, with [Thiago Alcântara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiago_Alc%C3%A2ntara "Thiago Alcântara") or any other central midfielder, dropping alongside Busquets to help progress the ball forward. Should the opposition press aggressively, the full-backs linked up to offer additional passing options as the center backs go deep and narrow. Wide forwards made diagonal runs into the midfield to link play with those in front of them. Once the ball was progressed out of the defense, they adjusted their attacking rhythm to match the opposition's defensive structure, either opting for a speedy transition against a higher block or relying on a more positional approach play against a lower block. To mix it up, Spain initially played short passes in the defensive-third before playing long to the center forward who then attempted to bring outfield runners in to play. Wing play was used to stretch opposition and create spaces infield or create crossing opportunities, especially against compact defenses.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-CW-98)
With Paris Saint-Germain, Luis Enrique continued to use an attacking 4–3–3 formation and continued to favour keeping the ball, but placed less emphasis on possession than in the past. He began to incorporate a bold new tactic at [kick-offs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kick-off_\(association_football\) "Kick-off \(association football\)"), where his team's striker would kick the ball out of play deep into the opposition half; during the ensuing throw-in, his team would then apply pressure to their opponents, through heavy pressing, in an attempt to win back the ball in attacking areas.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-104)[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-105) He made use of a balanced approach between attack and defence, with attacking full-backs that could assist at both ends of the pitch, while the movement of his front-three often disoriented opponents.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-106)
> "I do not treat all of my players the same, just as I do not treat all of my children the same. I have negotiated things with the players. On some things I have been permissive and on some I have been demanding. There are some rules that everyone must follow. That is one of my principles."
— Luis Enrique, speaking to the press after falling out with Messi in January 2015.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-107)
Known for his brave and fearless management style, Luis Enrique is quick to remove any influence that undermines his authority. Reports of his altercation with Messi at Barcelona and with Totti at Roma, both of whom wielded considerable power at their respective clubs, being prime examples of that.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-School-71) His flexibility in adopting different playing styles, while at odds with the [possession-based style](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiki-taka "Tiki-taka") synonymous with Barcelona, furthered this narrative, as he continued to remain unfazed in the face of criticism and pressure.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-FW-100) [Royal Spanish Football Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Spanish_Football_Federation "Royal Spanish Football Federation") president [Luis Rubiales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Rubiales "Luis Rubiales"), on the back of three consecutive unsuccessful tournaments, appointed him to curb ill-discipline and complacency in the squad, stating: "We are looking for an incontestable leader, who sets out the path, and nobody then strays from that path."[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-School-71)
Luis Enrique has also been known to drop or sell key players in his team whom he feels are not suited to his system or philosophy, as was the case with [Kylian Mbappé](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kylian_Mbapp%C3%A9 "Kylian Mbappé") and [Gianluigi Donnarumma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gianluigi_Donnarumma "Gianluigi Donnarumma") at Paris Saint-Germain.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-108)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-109)
### Reception
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luis_Enrique&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Reception")]
Messi described Luis Enrique as one of the two best managers he played for, the other being Guardiola.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-110) While Guardiola maintained that though he took on many great footballing sides as a head coach, Luis Enrique's Barcelona and [Jürgen Klopp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%BCrgen_Klopp "Jürgen Klopp")'s [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") were the best he ever faced.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-111)
In comparing the coaches he played for, Spain international Alcântara said: "[Luis Enrique] has the analytical positioning of Pep [and] the aggressiveness of Klopp", while also praising Luis Enrique's communication skills in conveying his footballing ideas.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-112)
### Relations with journalists
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luis_Enrique&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Relations with journalists")]
Luis Enrique had a strained relationship with journalists.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-113)[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-114) In September 2024, he claimed that he would gladly take a 50% cut in his salary if that meant he could avoid speaking to them.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-115)
## Endorsements
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luis_Enrique&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Endorsements")]
Luis Enrique was sponsored by sportswear company [Nike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nike,_Inc. "Nike, Inc."), and appeared in commercials for the brand. In a global advertising campaign in the run-up to the 2002 World Cup in South Korea and Japan, he starred in a "[Secret Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secret_Tournament "Secret Tournament")" commercial (branded "Scorpion KO") directed by [Terry Gilliam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry_Gilliam "Terry Gilliam"), appearing alongside footballers such as [Luís Figo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lu%C3%ADs_Figo "Luís Figo"), [Thierry Henry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thierry_Henry "Thierry Henry"), [Hidetoshi Nakata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hidetoshi_Nakata "Hidetoshi Nakata"), [Roberto Carlos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Carlos "Roberto Carlos"), [Ronaldinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronaldinho "Ronaldinho"), [Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronaldo_\(Brazilian_footballer\) "Ronaldo \(Brazilian footballer\)") and Totti, with former player [Eric Cantona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eric_Cantona "Eric Cantona") the tournament "referee".[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-116)
## Personal life
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Luis_Enrique&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Personal life")]
Luis Enrique married his longtime partner Elena Cullell on 27 December 1997.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-117) Their youngest daughter, Xana, died of [bone cancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone_tumor "Bone tumor") at age 9 on 29 August 2019;[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-118)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-119) they also had son Pacho (born 1998) and daughter Sira (2000), with the latter dedicating herself to [equestrianism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equestrianism "Equestrianism").[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-120)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-121)[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-122)
After retiring from football, Luis Enrique lived for a while in Australia to practice [surfing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surfing "Surfing"). He took part in the 2005 edition of the [New York City Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Marathon "New York City Marathon"), finished the [Amsterdam Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam_Marathon "Amsterdam Marathon") in 2006, the [Florence Marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florence_Marathon "Florence Marathon") in 2007 and the _[Marathon des Sables](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon_des_Sables "Marathon des Sables")_ in 2008, while also entering and finishing [Frankfurt Ironman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ironman_Germany "Ironman Germany") in 2007; he was due to take part in the [Ironman Triathlon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ironman_Triathlon "Ironman Triathlon") the following year, but eventually declined due to his engagement as manager of Barcelona B.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Enrique#cite_note-123)
